design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (service_repair_orders, env_0075) — design dossier.

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4,6,5,6]. Assignment: service_ext_owner_points_redemption 6, service_ext_paid_ro_points 6, service_ext_estimate_overage_credit 5, service_ext_month_end_points_expiry 4 (multiset {4,5,6,6} = draw).

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks one thing: put every Owner Rewards point on her CR-V's open repair order. The scored number (the 441.56 redemption credit she books herself) is the product of (a) a 6-factor redemption schedule (point value by tier and tenure, owner bonus from the CR-V's closed deal and Kessler Care plan, Kessler Shield bonus, the returned-payment hold, home-store and frequent-visit credits), (b) a points balance that is wrong at the opening in two directions — the paid Camry repair order RO 262107 never received its points, and the October month-end expiry has not been run — and (c) a points figure for RO 262107 that is itself wrong unless the estimate overage on that repair order is first credited back. The agent must read the redemption rule's two prerequisite sentences, find in the ledger that RO 262107 is paid without a points entry and that the October run is missing, then read the points rule's own prerequisite sentence and discover the overage on RO 262107 line A from the two authorization records. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling ~80 ledger rows and five cross-category holdings, and arithmetic — not from tool choice (each write has exactly one tool).

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed by task 0: service_ext_estimate_overage_credit (credit_estimate_overage_3db3cf5c), service_ext_paid_ro_points (credit_paid_ro_points_b77dd6a9), service_ext_month_end_points_expiry (expire_owner_points_a6cb3dc9), service_ext_owner_points_redemption (redeem_owner_points_3e3ce956, owner=user). Reserved headroom for task 1 (draw 3 prerequisites, factor counts [5,4,6,6]): the fleet side of the charter — diagnostic credit on an authorized repair, the customer's own estimate authorization, the early-payment discount on net terms and the comeback credit — none of which this task touches; task 1's world is a Commercial Fleet Account - Net 30, where none of task 0's points policies applies (points_earn_per_usd 0).

[Problem-tree card]
root d = service_ext_owner_points_redemption (on_request, USER tool).
edge d <- j (value_input, gate points_on_file, form state): policy_source "The redemption credit is fixed only after the records carry the points earned for every repair order on the account that has been paid in full and whose customer-pay labor charges, less the estimate overage, comeback, goodwill and rewards redemption credits on it, come to at least one dollar." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; waits on a record-visible state (a points-earned entry per paid repair order); no tool/id/code token; strength "every repair order ... paid in full" = condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a points-earned entry for a paid repair order: the paid-repair-order points policy (service_ext_paid_ro_points), whose rule says "The points are booked as one points-earned entry for the paid repair order". Seed evidence false at opening: RO 262107 payment row 2026-10-21 (937.30, card) and no service_points_earned row with repair_order_number RO 262107. Derivation: sentence + ledger (paid RO without points) + points rule -> credit points for RO 262107.
edge j <- h (value_input, gate paid_credits, form state): policy_source "The points for a paid repair order are fixed only after the records carry the overage credit owed on every line of it billed beyond its estimate tolerance." Connective "only after"; state = an estimate overage credit standing on the line; only the overage policy books credit_reason estimate_overage ("The overage credit is booked against the line's latest customer-pay labor charge as credit_reason estimate_overage"). False at opening: RO 262107 line A billed 526.32 + 391.40 = 917.72 vs authorized 612.40 + 186.54; no estimate_overage credit row on RO 262107.
edge d <- e (value_input, gate points_on_file, form action): policy_source "The redemption credit is not fixed until the month-end points expiry run for the latest calendar month whose last day falls on or before the redemption date has been made." Negated direction ("not ... until"). Action form (round 3), fallback_reason: A month-end run that finds no points expiring books no entry (an expiry entry always carries at least one point), so in such a month no record-visible state shows that the run was made; the wait is therefore stated on the run itself, which in such a month is made by working it out at no points. The waited-on action is the month-end run the expiry policy describes ("The month-end run for a calendar month is due on that month's last day; ... a run that finds no points expiring is made without an entry."), so exactly one write of this difficulty carries it: the points-expired entry of expire_owner_points_a6cb3dc9 when the run expires points. False at opening: frozen 2026-10-31 is the last day of October; the latest expiry entry is billing month 2026-07, no 2026-10 entry exists, and the October run expires 3,278 points (the 2024-06-15 points aged during October), so the run has not been made.
Topological order h, j, e, d; e commutes with h and j (replayed both orders: identical terminal state and values). Deletion sensitivity (run): skip j -> d 370.98; skip h -> j 5108; skip e -> d 480.54. User tool: the redemption is the customer's own disposal of her points; she runs it after the agent unlocks and hands it over. user_scenario names no prerequisite problem; the tools validate no prerequisite (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card]
step 12 (service_line_credited): governing base policies service_evt_diagnostic (authorized_within_window — RO 262107 line A diagnosed 2026-10-13, authorized 2026-10-14, Gold window 30 days inclusive, satisfied; one_diagnostic_credit — the only diagnostic credit on RO 262107 points at the diagnostic fee row, not at the labor row the overage credit points at), service_evt_estimate / payment_terms / rewards_points / goodwill (policy_scope), service_evt_comeback (within_repair_warranty — anchor the labor row 2026-10-20 at 50,410 miles; the credit is not a comeback, the window is not crossed). Overwrite: service_evt_estimate's tolerance sentence is retired on every account (round 2: the retail-only scope was dropped so no account is priced outside the policy); the replaced_by restates the tolerance, the further-authorization rule and credit_reason estimate_overage.
step 14 (service_points_earned): service_evt_rewards_points policy_scope; base earning sentence retired only for the repair order of the latest payment on a retail rewards account, restating the base for every other repair order (shop fees, late fees, deductibles and covered work still earn nothing).
step 16 (service_points_expired): service_evt_rewards_points and service_evt_account_close policy_scope (active_for_close applies only to closing). Base calendar-month expiry sentence retired only for the month-end run of an open retail rewards account; replaced by whole-month aging (the rule defines a whole month as complete on the same day of the following month, matching the record test exactly).
step 18 (service_points_redeemed): service_evt_rewards_points policy_scope; base point-value sentence retired only for a whole-balance redemption toward the open repair order; the minimum, whole points and the points_max_redemption_pct_of_ro cap are restated and the cap is kept in the computation (480.54, not reached).

[Business-object card] Target of the redemption: RO 262245 (CR-V, Kessler Honda Beavercreek, labor 402.48 + parts 558.60 + shop supplies 24.15, unpaid). Target of the points credit and the overage credit: RO 262107 (Camry): line A diagnostic fee 172.00 (credited 2026-10-14), labor 526.32 (row id in source_line_id), parts 391.40, shop supplies 31.58, rewards redemption credit 12.00 (1,200 points), card payment 937.30. Included in the overage: only line A's customer-pay labor and parts; the diagnostic fee and the shop fee are not "labor and parts". Excluded from points: shop fees, the diagnostic fee, the 12.00 points-paid portion. The other ten repair orders (RO 231874 ... RO 260819) are paid and carry their points entries; the March 2026 returned check on RO 260342 was re-paid by card on 2026-03-27 with the 30.00 returned payment fee.

[Factor card — values from the executed sensitivity run]
d (result 441.56, all-baseline 285.41): tenure_point_value -> 0.0125 (base 358.25); owner_vehicle_bonus (purchase + maintenance; CR-V deal closed + Kessler Care plan active) -> 0.16 (386.48); shield_holder_bonus (vsc; Exclusionary active) -> 0.05 (424.34); held_points_rule (method; returned check 2026-03-24) -> balance - 1000 (456.68); home_store_redemption_credit -> 10.00 (431.56); frequent_visit_redemption_credit (5 payments in 12 months) -> 15.00 (426.56). Near-miss: the Camry also has a closed deal but is not the redeeming vehicle; the CR-V is.
j (result 4666, all-baseline 1598): owner_earning_rate (purchase; Camry outside lender) -> 3 (3682); earning_dollars_rule (method; 12.00 redemption, paid 1 day after close) -> 787 (4711); shield_labor_bonus (vsc; Select active) -> 2 x 526 (3351); tenure_multiplier_rule -> 1.25 (3813); visit_frequency_bonus -> 250 (4416); care_member_bonus (maintenance) -> 150 (4516). Near-miss: the CR-V's deal is dealer-arranged (would give +2) but the paid repair order's vehicle is the Camry.
h (result 118.56, all-baseline 712.53): tenure_tolerance -> 0.05 (76.22); supplemental_decisions (method; two decisions, latest before close) -> 798.94 (800.16); owner_overage_courtesy (purchase) -> 15.00 (103.56); late_completion_courtesy (4 days) -> 20.00 (98.56); supplies_refund -> 0.06 (113.83). Near-miss: the diagnostic fee on line A is a customer-pay row but is not labor or parts.
e (result 3278, all-baseline 13866): care_plan_extension (maintenance) -> +6 (9658); shield_contract_extension (vsc) -> +3 (5620); used_points_order (method; 1,200-point redemption inside six months) -> 4621 used (2078); long_member_reserve -> 500 (3778). Near-miss: the 2024-08-09 points (2,342, 26 whole months) are aged under 24 months but not under 27.
Multi-source: every tier beyond the fall-through of every factor above combines the account's tier with a record condition (tenure, a cross-category holding, history count or date span). Cross-difficulty: purchase, maintenance and vsc holdings seeded for this customer (two closed deals, one active plan, two active contracts).

[Seed design] 13 repair orders 2023-11 .. 2026-10 priced with the Gold schedule (labor_rate_by_store KHB 172 / KTD 179, 10% labor discount capped 100 per repair order, 5% parts, 6% shop supplies capped 39.95, 4.95 hazardous waste, 1.0 diagnostic hour credited 100% inside 30 days), each customer-pay line authorized, each paid repair order carrying its points entry figured by the paid-repair-order schedule as it stood that day, month-end expiry entries (264 on 2026-03-31, 2,857 on 2026-07-31) figured by the expiry schedule as it stood each month (plan and contract extensions counted from the holdings' sale dates), a partial redemption (1,500 points, 15.00) on RO 250151 at points_value_usd (out of the whole-balance scope). Cross-category rows are holdings only (deals closed with their amounts and dates, plan priced 549 x 0.95 = 521.55 bundled, contracts inside their price caps). The CR-V's Kessler Care Plus 6-Visit plan KC-2408317 carries its plan ledger (round 7, SRC-2): 6 visits loaded 2024-04-20, 4 redeemed at Kessler Honda Beavercreek (RO 240717 2024-07-17 5,062 mi; RO 250120 2025-01-20 10,059; RO 250715 2025-07-15 14,965; RO 260622 2026-06-22 20,062 - odometers interpolated between the service readings, at least 60 days apart, near each 5,000-mile interval), so visits_remaining 2 = 6 - 4; the deals' and contracts' own ledgers are unread residue. open_balance 985.23 = RO 262245; rewards_points_balance 27153 = sum of points rows. Nothing else is owed: every older repair order is paid and pointed, diagnostic credits are booked, no repeat repair falls inside a repair warranty, the October run is the only one due.

[Persona] Diane Hartsfield, chatty Beavercreek librarian; volunteers only the surface goal and that she will pay the rest on Monday; gives phone and license last four on request (K=2), ZIP and email as extras; reads RO 262245 off her estimate sheet only when asked; describes vehicles and products only when asked; passive branches: lets the desk handle anything it says must come first, accepts held points, runs the redemption with the exact figures handed over, ends after the confirmation. She never mentions the Camry, its repair order, points owed, expiry or overage.

[Standard solution] Locate and verify (phone + 2386); read account, full ledger, authorizations, vehicles, stores, deals, plans, the plan ledger, contracts. Read the redemption rule: two prerequisite sentences -> RO 262107 paid without points; October run missing. Read the points rule: overage first -> RO 262107 line A 917.72 vs 798.94 x 1.05 -> credit 118.56 (step 12). Points for RO 262107 = 4666 (step 14). October expiry = 3278 (step 16). Hand over the redemption: 27,541 points, 441.56 on RO 262245 (step 18).

[Verification] The round-2 replay (scratch gt.py, deleted after use; t0world.py / t0task.py built the world in round 0) evaluates every computation with check_compute's own DSL on the replayed handling-time world (real task tools): h 118.56, j 4666, e 3278, d 441.56; per-factor baselines as listed; skip runs 370.98 / 5108 / 480.54; alternative order (e first) gives the identical terminal state. Draft recomputation from visible text only (policy prose + ledger + holdings + persona) reproduces the same four writes and values.

[Closure] policy -> tool -> step -> arg: h -> credit_estimate_overage_3db3cf5c step 12 credit_amount 118.56; j -> credit_paid_ro_points_b77dd6a9 step 14 points 4666; e -> expire_owner_points_a6cb3dc9 step 16 points 3278; d -> redeem_owner_points_3e3ce956 step 18 credit_amount 441.56 (user). charter_scope = required_documents = [h, j, e, d].

[Revisions] r1: e's base calendar-month convention replaced by whole-month aging (MONTHS() is a whole-month count; a calendar-month rule would differ on non-month-end days) and the run anchored to the last day of each month; frozen_time moved to 2026-10-31 so the October run is due today. r1: h, j scoped to the repair order of the latest payment and d to the open repair order (latest labor charge) — record tests stated in the rules and their self-naming scoped overwrites.


[Revisions r2] (audit revision_1) C-5: the redemption's wait on the expiry now reads 'The redemption credit is not fixed until the records carry the month-end points expiry of the latest calendar month whose last day falls on or before the redemption date.' and the expiry rule says its entry carries the month as its billing month; the base 'expiry month' concept is gone. C-2: every assembly sentence is generic (classes of adjustment in a fixed order, no factor quantity named). C-9: the overage rule names the vehicle only in the owner courtesy sentence. C-7a: the points rule tests paid in full (charges less credits less payments plus returned payments at zero or less) - RO 262107 stands at 0.00 before the overage credit and -118.56 after, so the points are owed. C-7d: every policy states the same-day tie rule (the record listed first counts). C-10: every 'last twelve whole months' window states its rolling convention (records dated today count). Rounding: rules, docstrings and tool bodies all round half up to the cent; the redemption's unrounded 438.115 is a half-cent tie and both the half-up tool and the DSL give 438.12. C-1: the overage policy now covers every account (fleet accounts take the 'another tier' tiers), so nothing is priced outside its scope. Proof text: owner_overage_courtesy and owner_earning_rate tier_taken now name the outside-lender tier this world takes. Values re-run unchanged: 118.56 / 4666 / 3278 / 438.12; skips 5108 (j<-h), 368.12 (d<-j; 368.13 from round 3 on, see below), 480.54 (d<-e). Window gate: the base diagnostic window sentence is now retired on every account by the diagnostic credit policy's declared overwrite (latest authorized decision on the line is the operative authorization), so step 12 no longer lists authorized_within_window as an inherited base gate; RO 262107's single authorization (2026-10-14, day 1 of 30) satisfies the replacement as well. Absent-record guards: every policy now states that with no reviewed object (no payment, no labor charge, no diagnostic fee, no earlier parts repair) it books nothing, and the compute returns 0 in those worlds instead of failing; the T0 values are unchanged. Whole months: every rule states that a whole month falling on a day the later month lacks completes on the first day of the month after.

[Revisions r3] (audit revision_2, task 0 PASS kept) N-1: the redemption's wait on the expiry is now in the action form - 'The redemption credit is not fixed until the month-end points expiry run for the latest calendar month whose last day falls on or before the redemption date has been made.' - with the fallback reason that a run expiring nothing books no entry; the expiry rule says such a run is made without an entry. On 2026-10-31 the October run expires 3,278 points, so the gold is unchanged. Zero-amount floors: the overage credit is never less than one cent where a line is billed beyond its tolerance, and a repair order paid in full on an earning tier earns at least one point, so neither write the redemption chain waits on can compute zero and be refused. Rounding: every money RND is RND(x + 0.000001, 2) (half up at exact ties); the d<-j skip run lands on an exact tie (368.125) and now reads 368.13 (Python round gave 368.12); the gold redemption 438.115 gives 438.12 both ways. Tools: line letters, the line of the named source row, points and amounts are parsed and enforced as their descriptions state; the module docstring says so. Gold values unchanged: 118.56 / 4666 / 3278 / 438.12; skips j<-h 5108, d<-j 368.13, d<-e 480.54.

[Revisions r4] (audit revision_3: task 0 PASS kept; coordinator rounding ruling) The redemption's raw figure 438.115 and three of its factor-sensitivity figures (453.115, 428.115, 423.115) sat exactly on a half cent (27,541 or 28,541 points x 0.015 per point), which the ruling forbids for scored, baseline and sensitivity figures. owner_plan_bonus_pct is now 0.16 (was 0.15): the redemption is 27,541 x 0.0125 x 1.21 + 10 + 15 = 441.557625 -> 441.56; sensitivities 358.25 / 386.48 / 424.34 / 456.68 / 431.56 / 426.56, all-baseline 285.41; skips d<-j 370.98, d<-e 480.54 (cap), j<-h 5108. Every scored, baseline and sensitivity figure of this task now sits more than 1e-6 from a half cent (checked: smallest distance 0.0005, shield_holder_bonus 424.3445). R-1: the expiry rule now states that a run not made on its month's last day is made on the day it is made, ageing points and counting every window to that day, with its entry dated that day and carrying the month the run is for; it is also never more than the points balance on file. The October run here is made on its due day (3,278 unchanged). R-3: the paid-RO points rule earns no points on a repair order whose customer-pay labor, less its overage, comeback, goodwill and redemption credits, is under one dollar (no one-point floor), and the redemption's wait on the points is carved to repair orders at or above that one dollar - RO 262107 (395.76) stays inside the wait. Rounding is RND(x + 0.000000001, 2); tools round with an exact decimal half-up helper and reject non-finite, exponent-form and non-integer inputs with an Error string (R-2).

[Revisions r6] (render_source render_r1) F1: paid in full now counts deductible charges too (rule and compute); RO 262107 carries none, so the points credit stays 4666. F4: held_points_rule reads its own account-age binding (enrollment_age_months) instead of tenure_point_value's months_open; values unchanged. EOC's booking row is stated as the line's latest customer-pay labor charge (RO 262107 line A, its only labor row). Gold values unchanged: 118.56 / 4666 / 3278 / 441.56.

[Revisions r7] (policy_kb SRC-2, seed only) The Kessler Care plan's visits remaining (2 of 6) is now reproducible from seeded plan-ledger rows (visits loaded at sale, four visits redeemed with repair order, store and odometer in date order), and the ledger is read in gold (find_maintenance_plan_ledger after find_maintenance_plans, so every later step number moved up by one: writes are steps 12, 14, 16 and 18). Charter and tools untouched; no factor reads the plan ledger (the plan factors read only the active status); gold values unchanged: 118.56 / 4666 / 3278 / 441.56.

[Revisions r8] (policy_kb SRC-3, SRC-6; seed and persona only) SRC-3: the two retail deals' holds now follow the purchase rules: KHB-24-21873 (New Vehicle Retail Purchase) reserved 2024-04-10 + 5 days = 2024-04-15, one +3-day extension -> hold_expires_date 2024-04-18 (the contract date), hold_extension_count 1; KTD-23-20946 (Certified Pre-Owned) reserved 2023-06-10 + 3 = 2023-06-13, its one +3-day extension -> 2023-06-16 (contract 2023-06-15), count 1; title applications (2024-04-24, 2023-06-21) were already inside 30 days of delivery. SRC-6: the CR-V's open repair order RO 262245 is now described in the persona as new front and rear brake pads and rotors - wear items the Factory Basic Limited Warranty lists as not covered, so customer pay is what the published coverage priority produces (2.6 flat-rate hours x 172.00 less 10% = 402.48; parts 588.00 list less 5% = 558.60, as seeded). No scored value moves: 118.56 / 4666 / 3278 / 441.56.

request_binding.action_semantics: A state-due credit: RO 262107 line A was billed 917.72 against authorized decisions of 612.40 and 186.54; the rule credits what was billed beyond the authorized amount plus tolerance. It is reached because the points of RO 262107, which the redemption waits on, are fixed only after this credit stands.

base_preconditions.condition: A diagnostic fee is credited at most once.
The overage credit settles customer-pay work billed on an authorized line beyond its tolerance; RO 262107 line A carries two authorized decisions and its labor and parts were billed on 2026-10-20.
Retail tiers pay each repair order at pickup; the credit lowers what is owed on a retail account and carries no net-terms consequence.
A rewards redemption credit already stands on RO 262107; the overage credit is a separate credit reason and is not a redemption.
A comeback credit is given only when the repeat repair falls within the repair warranty of the original customer-pay repair.
No goodwill credit is involved; the overage credit is owed under the estimate rule, not granted at discretion.

boundary_check.at_boundary: A repeat of this repair on 2027-10-20 would still be inside (inclusive); on 2027-10-21 outside.

edges.condition: Every repair order of the account paid in full whose customer-pay labor charges, less the estimate overage, comeback, goodwill and rewards redemption credits on it, come to at least one dollar carries its points-earned entry.
edges.policy_source: The redemption credit is fixed only after the records carry the points earned for every repair order on the account that has been paid in full and whose customer-pay labor charges, less the estimate overage, comeback, goodwill and rewards redemption credits on it, come to at least one dollar.

user_scenario: You are Diane Hartsfield, a fifty-eight-year-old school librarian from Beavercreek, Ohio, calling the Kessler Automotive Group service desk on the afternoon of Saturday, October 31, 2026. You are friendly and a little chatty, you like to have things explained once in plain words, and you are not in a hurry. Your 2024 Honda CR-V has been in at Kessler Honda Beavercreek for new front and rear brake pads and rotors; the advisor called to say it is finished and you are picking it up on Monday. You open the call by saying who you are and what you want: "I'd like to put every Owner Rewards point I have toward the repair order on my CR-V before I pick it up." You want the whole points balance used on that repair order, not just part of it, and you understand you will be the one to confirm the redemption yourself when the desk sets it up for you. You plan to pay whatever is left with your own card at the counter on Monday, so you do not want to make any payment on this call. You do not know how many points you have or what they are worth, and you have no idea how the desk works the credit out. When the desk asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 9375552741, and, if they want a second detail, the last four of your driver's license, 2386; if they ask for anything else you can also give your ZIP code, 45440, or your email, diane.hartsfield@outlook.com. Only if they ask for the repair order number do you read it off the estimate sheet in your purse: RO 262245. Only if they ask about your vehicles do you explain that the CR-V was bought new from Kessler Honda Beavercreek in April 2024 with a Kessler Care maintenance plan and a Kessler Shield contract, and that you also drive a 2021 Toyota Camry you bought certified from Kessler Toyota of Dayton in 2023, which has a Kessler Shield contract too. If the desk tells you something else has to be taken care of on your account before the points can go on the repair order, you tell them that is fine, they know their system better than you do, and you let them go ahead and handle it; you do not ask for details beyond a short explanation. If the desk tells you some of your points have to stay on the account and cannot be used today, you accept that without argument. When the desk tells you the number of points and the dollar credit and hands the redemption over to you, you complete it yourself for repair order RO 262245 using exactly the figures they gave you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once you see the redemption go through, you thank them warmly, mention you will see them Monday, and end the call.
